newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares surge 4.5 pct, buoyed by budget.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares surge 4.5 pct, buoyed by budget.

text.p: A string of market friendly steps announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget triggered heavy buying on the Delhi bourse during a special trading session, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index shot up 33.55 points, or 4.5 percent, to close at 779.96 in a special post-budget trading session.
"The finance minister, P. Chidambaram, has accepted most of the recommendations made by the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) which is more than we expected," said DSE president Paramjit Singh.
"The proposal to hike foreign institutional investors (FIIs) investment from the existing 24 percent to 30 percent would increase the flow of FII investment into the country," Singh added.
Chidambaram proposed in the 1997/98 budget to raise investment limits in firms for FIIs, non-resident Indians and overseas corporate bodies to 30 percent from 24 percent.
Reliance Industries rose 22 rupees to 294.50 on increased demand from FIIs and speculators, brokers said.
TISCO firmed up from a pre-budget close of 192.10 rupees to 203.30.
Cement maker ACC shot up 72 rupees to 1,565 on buying by speculators and Bombay-based traders, brokers said.
ITC Ltd gained 18.40 at 425 while Hindustan Lever moved up from 905 rupees to close at 940 on buying by FIIs and domestic financial institutions.
Larsen and Toubro rose 10.35 rupees to 252.
Bajaj Auto Ltd increased 35 rupees at 940.
